MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. Duplicates are not removed from the combined set.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: UnionAll

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains a unique list of objects that includes objects returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. The combined set will not contain duplicates.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: UnionUnique

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left as well as the right search definition operand.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: Intersection

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left but not from the right search definition operand.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: Difference

MetaEnum.description:
Set operator values to use when combining the results from each search definition in a ExpressionGroupInput.
    • UnionAll     - Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. Duplicates are not removed from the combined set.
    • UnionUnique -    Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains a unique list of objects that includes objects returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. The combined set will not contain duplicates.
    • Intersection -    Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left as well as the right search definition operand.
    • Difference    - Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left but not from the right search definition operand.
MetaEnum.name: SearchGroupOperator

MetaEnum.description:
Join operator values to use when combining the results from each search definition in a ExpressionJoinInput.

    • InnerJoin - Combines the column values of two searches (A and B) based upon a join condition. The join compares each row of A with each row of B to find all pairs of rows which satisfy the join condition.
    • LeftJoin - The result of a left join for searches A and B always contains all records of the "left" search (A), even if the join condition does not find any matching record in the "right" search (B).
    • RightJoin - The result of a right join for searches A and B always contains all records of the "right" search (B), even if the join condition doesn't find any matching record in the "left" search (A).
    • FullJoin - The result of a full join for searches A and B always contains all records of both searches. Where records in A and B don't match, the result set will have NULL values for every column of the search that lacks a matching row. For those records that do match, a single row will be produced in the result set (containing fields populated from both searches).
MetaEnum.name: SearchJoinOperator

MetaEnum.description: Sort operator values which decide the sort order for attributes in Search Options
MetaEnum.name: SortOperator

ParameterInfo.description: A list of VariantRule with which each variant condition is validated. The subclasses of the VariantRule are also allowed, for instance, Cfg0VariantCriteria.
A list of Conditions that need to be validated.
A map (string, string) of request names and value pairs. This is for future use; leave empty.

Operation.description: This operation solves each condition in a list with each VariantRule in a list. Each variant condition in the condition is validated against each VariantRule. Each VariantRule in the list can have different configurator context and different configurations like RevionRule, RuleDate, and Effectivity. This operation requires tc_ipd_config_gtwy license.
Operation.name: batchSolveConditions
Operation.returnDescription:
The operation returns a list of solve results for each variant condition. The list of solve results and the list of input, that is, VariantRule objects and variant conditions will be in the same sequence.

Following partial errors may be returned.
26025 - No Flexlm license is available for Teamcenter optional module ‘tc_ipd_config_gtwy’.
26026 - No Flexlm license is available for Teamcenter concurrent module ‘tc_ipd_config_gtwy’.
77173 - The variantRules list contains a null element at index ‘number’.
77174 - The VariantRule at index ‘number’ is missing a configurator perspective or a solve profile or both.
77175 - The list of variant conditions cannot be empty.
77176 - The formula string of index conditionExpressions ‘number’, of index conditions ‘number’, cannot be converted into an expression.
Operation.useCase:
Use case 1:
Apply a VariantRule on a list of variant conditions. Some variant conditions will be configured in and some others will be configured out.

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRule1 ]
conditions = [ conditionExpressions1, conditionExpressions2, conditionExpressions2 ]
conditionExpressions1 = [ expressionInfo1 ]
expressionInfo1 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & B=b1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}
conditionExpressions2 = [ expressionInfo2 ]
expressionInfo2 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & C=c1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}
conditionExpressions3 = [ expressionInfo3 ]
expressionInfo3 = { variantFormula : "", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}

Response:
solveResults[0] = { [ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2, conditionsStatus3 ], isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus3[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ]


Use case 2:
Solve a list of variant conditions with each VariantRule in a list of VariantRule. Some variant conditions will be configured in and some others will be configured out for each VariantRule. All the VariantRule objects in the list have the same configurator Context.

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRule1, variantRule2 ]
conditions = [ conditionExpressions1, conditionExpressions2 ]
conditionExpressions1 = [ expressionInfo1 ]
expressionInfo1 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & B=b1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}
conditionExpressions2 = [ expressionInfo2 ]
expressionInfo1 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & C=c1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}

Response:
For variantRule1:
solveResults[0] = { [ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2 ] , isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]

For variantRule2:
solveResults[1] = { [ conditionsStatus3, conditionsStatus4 ] , isValid = false, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus3[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus4[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]

Use case 3:
Solve a list of variant conditions with each VariantRule in a list of VariantRule. Some variant conditions will be configured in and some others will be configured out for each VariantRule. All the VariantRule objects in the list have different Configurator Context.

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRuleWithContexA, variantRuleWithContexB ]
conditions = [ conditionExpressions1, conditionExpressions2 ]
conditionExpressions1 = [ expressionInfo1 ]
expressionInfo1 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & B=b1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}
conditionExpressions2 = [ expressionInfo2 ]
expressionInfo2 = { variantFormula : "A=a1 & C=c1", effectivityFormula : "", jsonExpression : ""}

Response:
For variantRuleWithContexA:
solveResults[0] = { [ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2 ], isValid = true, isComplete = true }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]

For variantRuleWithContexB:
solveResults[1] = { [ conditionsStatus3, conditionsStatus4 ], isValid = false, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus3[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]
conditionsStatus4[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ]

Use case 4:
You want to do an overlay solve with more than one VariantRule. This use case can be achieved with
two approaches as explained below.

Approach 1:
You need to invoke the operation with a first VariantRule and a list of variant conditions. Invoke the operation again with a second VariantRule and configured-out variant conditions from the first VariantRule. The overlay solve result is a union of configured-in variant conditions from both operation responses. This approach needs to invoke operation twice however has the advantage of fewer solve operations in the second time calling the operation.

Step1 - Call the batchSolveConditions operation with the following inputs

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRule1 ]
conditions = [ VC1, VC2, VC3, VC4,VC5 ]

Response:
solveResults[0] = { [ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2,conditionsStatus3, conditionsStatus4, conditionsStatus5 ], isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC1
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC2
conditionsStatus3[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC3
conditionsStatus4[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC4
conditionsStatus5[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC5

From a list of conditionsStatus, get a valid list, that is configured in and an invalid list, that is configured out.
ValidList1 = [ VC1,VC2, VC4 ]
InvalidList1 = [ VC3,VC5 ]

Step2 - Call the batchSolveConditions with the following inputs

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRule2 ]
conditions = [ VC3,VC5 ] InvalidList1 from step1

Response:
solveResults[0] = {[ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2 ], isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC3
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC5

From a list of conditionsStatus, get valid list, that is configured in
ValidList2 = [ VC5 ]
InvalidList2 = [ VC3 ]

Overlay Solve Result = ValidList from step1 and step2
[ VC1,VC2, VC4 ] + [ VC5 ]

Approach 2:
You need to invoke the operation with both VariantRule objects and a list of variant conditions. The overlay solve result is a union of configured-in variant conditions from the first VariantRule and an intersection of Configured-out variant conditions from the first VariantRule and Configured-in variant conditions from the second VariantRule. This approach needs a single call to the operation. However, you need to identify the overlay solve result as explained, and also the operation has more number of solve operations.

Request:
variantRules = [ variantRule1, variantRule2 ]
conditions = [ VC1, VC2, VC3, VC4,VC5 ]

Response:
solveResults[0] = {[ conditionsStatus1, conditionsStatus2,conditionsStatus3, conditionsStatus4, conditionsStatus5 ], isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus1[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC1
conditionsStatus2[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC2
conditionsStatus3[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC3
conditionsStatus4[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC4
conditionsStatus5[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC5

From a list of conditionsStatus, get valid list, that is configured in and invalid list, that is configured out.
ValidList1 = [ VC1,VC2, VC4 ]
InvalidList1 = [ VC3,VC5 ]

solveResults[1] = {[ conditionsStatus6, conditionsStatus7,conditionsStatus8, conditionsStatus9, conditionsStatus10 ], isValid = true, isComplete = false }
conditionsStatus6[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC1
conditionsStatus7[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC2
conditionsStatus8[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ false ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC3
conditionsStatus9[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC4
conditionsStatus10[0] = [ { isConfigured : [ true ], explanation: ""} ] -> for VC5

From a list of conditionsStatus, get valid list, that is configured in and invalid list, that is configured out.
ValidList2 = [ VC2, VC4, VC5 ]
InvalidList2 = [ VC1, VC3 ]

Solve Result = ValidList1 and intersection of InvalidList1 and ValidList2
[ VC1,VC2, VC4 ] + [ VC5 ]

The string "NS" is the family namespace. The family namespace defines the uniqueness of the family within itself. System ensures that the combination of the family namespace and the family id is unique in the database. For family "F" with namespace "NS" system will identify it as "[NS]F".

The examples of display formulae are as follows:

1) Boolean expression

[NS]BOOL - represents TRUE
[NS]!BOOL - represents FALSE


2) Date expressions
Date features are displayed in the standard Teamcenter locale-specific date format.
3) Range expressions

[NS]A = a1 & [NS]LENGTH <= 50
[NS]A = a1 & ([NS]LENGTH >= 1 & [NS]LENGTH <= 10)
[NS]A = a1 & [NS]LENGTH >= 20
[NS]A = a1 & !([NS]LENGTH >= 20)


4) Multiple column expressions must be grouped within brackets

([NS]A = a1 & [NS]B = b1) | ([NS]A = a2 & [NS]C = c1)


5) Multiple selections within a single column

([NS]A = a1 | [NS]A = a2) & [NS]B = b1


6) Multiple selections in a family 'C' that has Multi-select=Yes

([NS]A = a1 | [NS]A = a2) & [NS]C = c1 & [NS]C = c2


7) Optional family 'D' [Target]

[NS]A = a1 & [NS]D = NONE (same as [NS]D = '')
[NS]A = a1 & [NS]D = ANY (same as [NS]D != '')

ParameterInfo.description: A Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective is a runtime business object representing a snapshot of a Configurator Product Context object. The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.

This string should adhere to the JSON schema for solve profile defined in SolveProfile_Schema.json; please refer to schema and sample solve profiles defined at %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema for details. • "maxSize" : It is a maximum number of the buildable combinations to generate. The default value is 10000. A value for maxSize should be less than or equal to 10000.

ParameterInfo.description:
This parameter indicates the time from which unprocessed data is to be retrieved from a data grid. This data will be processed into a smaller subset i.e. condensed form.
The format is in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
The time is closed interval.
If the startTime is not provided, the time interval will be determined based on the Teamcenter preference i.e. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval.
Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval takes string value in the format of PnYnMnDTnHnMnS as defined in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601

This parameter indicates the time up to which unprocessed data is to be retrieved from a data grid. This data will be processed into a smaller subset i.e. condensed form.
The format is in ISO 8601 format https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
The time is closed interval.
If the endTime is not provided, the time interval will be determined based on a Teamcenter preference i.e. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval takes string value in the format of PnYnMnDTnHnMnS as defined in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
A map (string, list of string). This is reserved for future use.

Operation.description:
•    The generateCondensedTelemetry service operation retrieves a large dataset from the data grid and processes it into a smaller subset, which is used to generate a configurator data snapshot. Data grid is a key-value store database.
•    This condensed telemetry data is then posted back to the data grid for snapshot generation.
•    The resulting snapshot provides downstream users with consistent configurator data, enabling faster response times and improved user experience.
•    At present, the end user cannot see the condensed telemetry data on the data grid.

Overview when the service operation is executed successfully:
•    When the data condensation for the specified time interval is successful, the condensed telemetry data is posted to the data grid. The data grid will store this condensed telemetry data, which will later be used in subsequent operations for snapshot generation.
•    Once the condensed telemetry data is posted to the data grid, the server will track the number of jobs that have been posted for snapshot generation. This count is returned in the service operation response under the parameter "numberOfJobs."
•    Absence of any partial errors in serviceData represents the successful completion of the service operation.

Overview when the service operation execution fails:
•    If the service operation fails for any reason, no data will be posted to the data grid. The value "numberOfJobs" will be returned as 0.
•    The serviceData will have the partial errors to indicate the failure of the service operation.
Operation.name: generateCondensedTelemetry
Operation.returnDescription:
The operation will return a structure specifying the status of the operation and number of jobs to be processed for snapshot generation.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    77089 - The request to compile a Configurator Rule Set was not processed, because the specified date “startTime” represents a date in the future. Please use a date before the current date "2024-11-14T00:00:00Z ".
•    77213 - The request to compile a Configurator Rule Set was not processed, because the specified date “startTime” is greater than “endTime”.
Operation.useCase:
Use case 1:
In this use case, user wants to download and condense telemetry data from the data grid for a specific time period. The time period is specified against the parameters "startTime" and "endTime". The downloaded data will be processed and condensed into a smaller subset.
The operation returns "numberOfJobs" as 100, which means there are 100 jobs for generating configurator snapshot. There are no partial errors in the “serviceData” which means the operation was successful.
Input:    
    startTime : 2024-06-06T00:00:00Z
    endTime : 2024-11-06T00:00:00Z
Output:
    numberOfJobs: 100    

Use case 2:
In this use case, user wants to download and condense telemetry data from the data grid for a specific time period. The time period is specified against the parameters "startTime" and "endTime". Here, the "startTime" and "endTime" are in the future.
The “serviceData” will have partial errors specifying that the "startTime" and "endTime" are in the future. The operation returns "numberOfJobs" as 0, because the operation has failed.
Input:    
    startTime : 2030-06-06T00:00:00Z
    endTime : 2030-11-06T00:00:00Z
Output:
    numberOfJobs: 0
    serviceData : Partial errors containing error with code 77089.

Use case 3:
In this use case, user wants to download and condense telemetry data from the data grid for a specific time period. But the parameter "endTime" is not given. So, the time interval for downloading data is based on the Teamcenter preference i.e. cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval.
Let’s consider the value of Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval is set to “P6M". The system will download data from the past 6 months up to the current time on the clock. The downloaded data will be processed and condensed into a smaller subset.
The operation returns "numberOfJobs" as 200, which means there are 200 jobs for generating configurator snapshot.
Input:    
    startTime : 2024-06-06T00:00:00Z
    endTime :
Output:
    numberOfJobs: 200

Use case 4:

Operation.description:
•    The generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operation retrieves the condensed telemetry data from the data grid and processes it to generate a configurator snapshot. Data grid is a key-value store database.
•    The generated configurator snapshot is posted back to the data grid.
•    Each service operation will be assigned one telemetry job from the data grid and processes it to generate configurator snapshot. There will be parallel invocation of generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operations to multiple servers.
•    The configurator snapshot enables the downstream users to work with a pre-processed constant or frozen configurator data. This enables improved performance for validate and expand action.

The service operation retrieves a job from the data grid based on priority, as determined by the generateCondensedTelemetry service operation. A job corresponds to a single row in the data grid, containing condensed telemetry data used to generate the configurator snapshot.

Each job in the data grid has a status value of "Pending," indicating that it is available for processing. The service operation will be assigned one of these "Pending" jobs for processing.

The assignment of a job to the service operation is not based on any input to the service operation. Therefore, the service operation does not take any input parameters except requestInfo.

Overview when the service operation is executed successfully:
•    The service operation retrieves a specific row of condensed telemetry data from the data grid. This row of condensed telemetry is called a ‘job’.
•    If the job retrieval is successful, the data grid is updated for that particular row. This update helps to determine which job will be selected from the data grid for snapshot generation in the next service operation request by another server.
•    The server generates a snapshot for the retrieved job. After each successful job completion, the status of the job on the data grid will be marked as complete.
•    If there are any more unprocessed jobs on the data grid then in the response, the value of moreJobsExist is true, more service operations are to be invoked. If false, no more service operations are to be invoked.

Overview when the service operation execution fails:
•    The service operation will retrieve a specific row of condensed telemetry data from the data grid. This row of condensed telemetry is called a ‘job’.
•    If job retrieval fails due to the absence of unprocessed jobs in the data grid, the moreJobsExist value will be set to false, along with an error in the serviceData. For any other unexpected failure, an appropriate error will be reported in the serviceData.
•    The server will try to generate a snapshot for the retrieved job. In case of failure, the status of the job on the data grid will be not be marked as complete. In this case, the job is again available for processing by the next service operation request.
•    If a job is taking more time than what is defined in the preference cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval then it will be marked as ‘timed out’.
•    If a job is getting failed for a maximum 5 number of times then it will be marked as ‘timed out’ in the data grid. The timed out jobs will not be picked by the service operation for processing.
Operation.name: generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot
Operation.returnDescription:
The operation will return a structure specifying whether there are any more pending jobs on the data grid.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    77214 - There are no unprocessed jobs on the data grid.
Operation.useCase:
Use case 1:
In this use case, generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operation is tasked with creating a configurator snapshot for a given job. After successfully generating the snapshot, there are additional unprocessed jobs in the data grid. As a result, the moreJobsExist flag is set to true, and there are no errors reported in the serviceData.
a.    Triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator:
    • The user initiates the process by triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator, a Java application designed to process jobs in parallel present on the data grid.
    • The TcFtsIndexer_configurator calls the service operation generateCondensedTelemetry.


b.    Service Operation: generateCondensedTelemetry:
    • The service operation generateCondensedTelemetry downloads the telemetry data from the data grid and condenses it.
    • After condensing the telemetry data, the service operation posts the condensed data back to the data grid in the form of jobs.
    • Response: The service returns the number of unprocessed jobs currently on the data grid.


c.    Re-triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator:
    • The TcFtsIndexer_configurator is triggered again to process the jobs.


d.    Service Operation: generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot:
    • This time, the service operation generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot is called by the TcFtsIndexer_configurator.
    • The service operation is assigned a specific job from the data grid, which it processes to generate configurator snapshot.
    • Response: Since more jobs exist, the moreJobsExist field is set to true. There are no errors in the serviceData.


Use case 2:
In this use case, generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operation is tasked with creating a configurator snapshot for a given job. After successfully generating the snapshot, no additional unprocessed jobs remain in the data grid. As a result, the moreJobsExist flag is set to false, and there are no errors reported in the serviceData.
a.    Triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator:
    • The user initiates the process by triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator, a Java application designed to execute tasks in parallel on the data grid.
    • The TcFtsIndexer_configurator calls the service operation generateCondensedTelemetry.


b.    Service Operation: generateCondensedTelemetry:
    • The service operation generateCondensedTelemetry downloads the telemetry data from the data grid and condenses it.
    • After condensing the telemetry data, the service operation posts the condensed data back to the data grid in the form of jobs.
    • Response: The service returns the number of unprocessed jobs currently on the data grid.


c.    Re-triggering the TcFtsIndexer_configurator:
    • TcFtsIndexer_configurator is triggered again to process the job


d.    Service Operation: generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot:
    • This time, the service operation generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot is called by the TcFtsIndexer_configurator.
    • The service operation is assigned a specific job from the data grid, which it processes to generate configurator snapshot.
    • Response: In this use case, no more jobs exist so the value of moreJobsExist is set to false. There are no errors in the serviceData.

    
Use case 3:
In this use case, generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot is called by the TcFtsIndexer_configurator but there are no unprocessed jobs in the data grid. The service operation will throw error in this use case.
a.    TcFtsIndexer_configurator:
    • In this use case, the TcFtsIndexer_configurator is triggered to process the condensed telemetry jobs.


b.    Service Operation: generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot:
    • This time, the service operation generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot is called by the TcFtsIndexer_configurator.
    • There are no unprocessed jobs on the data grid.
    • Response: The value of moreJobsExist field is set to false. “serviceData” will contain error with code 77214.

Operation.description: This operation returns the admissibility statements for the variability data associated with a given set of context objects. The instance of Cfg0AbsAdmissibility object represents the relation and state between a configurator specific object and a non-configurator specific object. For example, the pair of a partition and an family is associated with state "Available". The admissibility states are defined by the LOV Cfg0AdmissibilityState. The allowed values for this property are "Available" and "Not Available".
Operation.exceptionCondition: The operation will return a ServiceException if an unknown error occurs. A possible source for unknown errors could be a codeful configurator component customization.

ParameterInfo.description: It is the object containing input information required to compute the available product variability.

Operation.description: This operation computes the available features within a set of requested families. The parameters criteriaExpression and familiesToTest are used to pass in the input expression and families of interest requesting the available features. The operation in response returns the available product variability for the requested families satisfying the input expression in criteriaExpression and the constraint(s) present in the system. If the input parameter criteriaExpression is empty, then the response will return the product variability for the requested families satisfying all the system constraints. If the requested family list is empty, the operation will not return any variability information.
Operation.name: getAvailableProductVariability
Operation.returnDescription:
A list of variant features, default features, value ranges, violations and/or the suggested expression satisfying input expression and the set of constraints present in the configurator context.

The following partial errors may be returned:
79010 Must provide at least one product item in the configuration perspective.
79009 An invalid configuration .
79012 The target family container is empty.
256054 The value for the applyConstraints bit pattern is invalid. Please refer to documentation for valid values.

ParameterInfo.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective business object that represents a snapshot of a Product Context object. The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.

The configuration solve profile as JSON string that consists of attributes governing the behavior of configurator constraint evaluation. This string should adhere to the JSON schema for solve profile defined in SolveProfile_Schema.json; please refer to schema and sample solve profiles defined at %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema for details. Each solve profile key should occur only once in the solve profile JSON string.
The input criteria expression based on which the available variability is to be computed. The service operation allows only precise criteria expression to be passed in the input.
A list of families from the same product context to get the available features. At least one family of interest should be present in the input.
A list of request names and value pairs. This is reserved for future use.

Operation.description:
This operation computes the available variability for a set of requested families which satisfies the input expression against the constraint(s) present in the system. The operation allows only precise expression to be passed as input in order to get the available variability for the requested families.
A precise expression represents a single product configuration and does not allow multipe values for mutually exclusive single select families. For example, if A1, A2 and A3 are values of single select family A and B1 and B2 are values of single select family B, the expression (A=A1 & B=B1) is a precise expression, whereas the following expressions are imprecise and are not supported by the operation:
1.    (A=A1 & B=B1) | (A=A2 & B=B2) - Multiple product configurations.
2.    (A=A1 | A=A2) & (B=B1 | B=B2) - Multiple feature values are selected from mutually exclusive family.
3.    A!=A3 – Expression equals (A=A1 | A=A2), that is multiple feature values selected from single select family.

If the input expression is empty, then the operation will return the available variability for the product against the constraint(s) present in the system.
The operation returns criteria status which represents the status of the configuration as part of response; the completeness of the configuration is irrespective of the families of interest and considers all the families present for the provided product context. In order to get the list of families missing valid selections for valid and incomplete configuration or details of violations for invalid configuration, the validateAndExpandExpressions service operation should be called.

Below keys are specific to the current operation:

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_skipSolutionSeverityProcessing” is set to true, the system will not compute constraint severity for each expanded expression terms. Else the system will compute constraint severity for each expanded expression terms. Computing constraint severity is performance intensive operation. Example below Use case 5 and Use case 5.1.

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_computeRangeForFreeFormFamily” is set to true, the valid range computation of free form values will be done, else valid range computation will not be done and existing range on a family without considering constraints will be returned. Example below Use case 6 and Use Case 6.1.

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_getAllAvailableValuesPerFamily” is set to true, the system will get available values for each requested family individually after resetting clause of current family from the input expression. If user has this key set to false, the available values for each requested family are computed considering input expression as constraint. Example below Use case 7 and Use case 7.1.

This operation requires tc_ipd_config_gtwy license.
Operation.name: getAvailableVariability
Operation.returnDescription:
The available variability for the families of interest, the expanded expression and criteria status of the configuration.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    26025 - No Flexlm license is available for Teamcenter optional module ‘tc_ipd_config_gtwy’.
•    77073 - The Configurator Perspective is inavalid.
•    77074 - The Configurator Perspective must contain a product item.
•    77075 - At least one Family is expected in the input.
•    77143 - The JSON schema validation for “solveProfile” has failed.
•    77170 - The input criteria expression is imprecise, because multiple product configurations exist.
•    77171 - The input criteria expression is imprecise, because multiple features are selected from single select mutually exclusive family “A”.
•    77172 - The input criteria expression is imprecise, because it contains “NOT” operator for single select mutually exclusive family “A”.
•    256021 - The string ‘text’ cannot be converted into an expression.
•    256055 - The provided solve profile is invalid.
•    256059 - The input solve profile JSON is invalid because it consists of duplicate key “CFG_PROFILE_applyConfigConstraints”.

79014 - The operation has failed to retrieve configuration information for VariantRule at index “n”.

ParameterInfo.description: Contains input required to perform solution completeness check for a given set of combinations.

Operation.description:
The Service operation expects a user to provide a set of configurations which are to be checked for validity and completeness. The service operation also returns a set of configurations which are unknown to the user.

These configurations are passed to and returned by the service operation via a ‘Roster Table’.

A ‘Roster Table’ is used to represent configurations. A ‘Roster Table’ is capable of storing configurations. A configuration record in ‘Roster Table’ is similar to saved variant rule. ‘Roster Table’ consists of two parts,

1.    Column Headers – A list of config expressions, one for each column in the table. A config expression is used to identify family name, family namespace, value and operator. Example: In the config Expression “[Teamcenter]A=A1”, family name is A, namespace is “Teamcenter”, operator is “=” and operand is “A1”.

2.    Rows – Rows store multiple row. A row contains a configuration, just like a Saved Variant Rule. The configuration is stored in a bit string, which means it can only contain ‘0’ or ‘1’. The total length of bit string is twice the number of columns present in ‘Roster Table’. Hence a string representing a cell has a size of 2. Given string can only have either ‘0’ or ‘1’ the following strings can represent a cell. They are described below with their logical meaning
    a.    ‘00’ – Both True and False conditions are possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    b.    ‘01’ – Only True condition is possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    c.    ‘10’ – Only False Condition is possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    d.    ‘11’ - Not Defined

A user input consisting of one/more configurations is passed to the service operation using ‘Roster Table’. These configurations are checked by the service operation for validity and completeness. An input ‘Roster Table’ is said to be complete if the input ‘Roster Table’ passed by user is able to represent all the possible combinations given no constraint is violated.

User has ability to provide scope to the service operation while doing completeness check. This is done by passing a list of families. Only families present in the list are used by the service operation to compute the possible combinations and then evaluate whether the passed configurations via input ‘Roster Table’ are able to cover each and every one of them.

User also has an ability to provide ‘explicit families’ to service operation. When a configuration from input ‘Roster Table’ is checked for validity turns out to be ‘invalid’ then service operation checks weather the reason for its invalidity is due to a family present in ‘explicit families’. If yes, then exception conditions on those family is checked, if we find an exception condition that meets the configuration input this implies the exception condition allows the configuration to be valid.

Given all configurations passed via input ‘Roster Table’ are valid, and they are able to represent all possible combinations then input is said to be complete. If they don’t the configurations passed via input ‘Roster Table’ are termed incomplete. Missing configurations are computed by service operation and returned via output ‘Roster Table’

If some but not all configuration passed by user via ‘Roster Table’ is found to be invalid, this means that the configuration wasn’t able to satisfy constraints present in the system. User can specify severity of constraints which will participate in evaluating the configurations in input ‘Roster Table’. These invalid configurations are communicated back to the user and missing configurations are evaluated using valid configurations present in input ‘Roster Table’.

If all the configurations passed to the service operation are invalid the service operation will return empty output ‘Roster Table’.

Use Case 1:
A product context has 3 Boolean Families ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’.

These 3 families can create a total of 8 configurations given there is no constraint in the system.

A user can use ‘getConfigurationRosterCoverage’ service operation to pass 3 configuration among the 8 possible via input ‘Roster Table’.

In the current example all the 8 configurations are possible but the user only passed 3 of them in input. Hence the service operation provides verdict as ‘valid’ for all the 3 input configurations. The remaining 5 configurations are returned back to user via output ‘Roster Table’. Additionally service operation also returns a verdict of ‘incomplete’ to user as he missed 5 possible configurations in input ‘Roster Table’.
Operation.name: getConfigurationRosterCoverage
Operation.returnDescription:
Output structure tells user which combinations passed in input via ‘Roster Table’ were valid and which were invalid. Additionally if also informs user how a correction can be made to an invalid input configuration such that it becomes a valid configuration.

The following partial errors may be returned:
•    79001 - The operation has encountered an internal error.

ParameterInfo.description: List of objects of type VariantRule or Cfg0AbsConfiguratorCriteria from which the Product Configurator configuration session information needs to be retrieved.

Operation.description: This operation retrieves the Product Configurator configuration session information from the objects that are marked to carry such information. User starts a Product Configurator session to create product configurations using configuration features. The session holds product information such as the, Cfg0ConfContext, RevisionRule, Effectivity, Rule Date. The product information is also represented as Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective object. The product information configures the features which user can select to build product configuration. The session also holds parameters called as Configuration Profile which govern the evaluation of configurator constraints during validation and expansion of the product configuration. The objects must implement ConfigurationSession behavior, so that Product Configurator configuration session information can be attached and retrieved from them.
Operation.name: getConfigurationSessionInfo
Operation.returnDescription:
Returns a list of configuration session information structures where each session information structure holds a product information to select the features and constraints as a Configurator Perspective and parameters to govern the constraint evaluation as Configuration Profile. The input list of objects is processed in sequence. If operation fails to retrieve session information for an input object, a partial error is returned for the same and the processing continues for the next object in the list.

The partial errors are returned in serviceData in following cases:

77103 - The operation has failed, because the input object is not session configurable.
Operation.useCase: User wants to view a Configurator Criteria which has the Product Configurator configuration session information attached. User may use this information to apply the product configuration associated with the Configurator Criteria on product content and configure it. The session information will recreate the Product Configurator configuration session with features and constraints against which the product content configuration will be evaluated.

    • 79010 - The operation "getContextBasedVariantExpressions" expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
    • 77061 - An invalid revision rule provided to the operation.
Operation.useCase:
Use case 1 :
User can get variant expressions of an existing object. For example

Create an instance of default rule (Cfg0DefaultRule) by using operation setVariantExpressions and set subject condition as "Color = Red". To retrieve this variant expression getContextBasedVariantExpressions can be used which returns variant expression formula and the client representable structure format.

Use case 2:
If Option Value is not allocated in the input Configurator Context, only the Value text is returned in response, Option tag is empty. For Example,

Create an instance of inclusion rule (Cfg0InclusionRule) under Context1 with following subject and applicability:
Subject: Transmission = Manual (Manual is allocated to both Context1 and Context2)
Applicability: Engine = V4 (V4 is allocated to only Context1)
Now allocate the Inclusion Rule to Context2. Open Inclusion Rule from Context2 in Expression Editor. Option V4 is shown as Read Only Text.

This operation can be used to retrieve rules for the given product item(s) or product model(s) from parameter context. Parameter filterCriteria can be used for filtering based on specific family group(s) or family (families) or feature(s).

Family Groups:
Engine-Box - It has families "Engine" and "Transmission".
Engine - Petrol, Diesel
Transmission - Manual, Auto
Wheel - It has families "Wheel-drive" and "Suspension".
Wheel-drive - 2-Wheels, 4-Wheels
Suspension - Full-Thrust, Full-Boom

The rules are created as follows

1.If Transmission=Manual Then Set Wheel-drive=2-Wheels.
2.If Transmission=Auto Then Set Wheel-drive=4-Wheels.
3.If Engine=Diesel And Transmission=Manual Then Set Suspension=Full-Thrust.
4.If Engine=Petrol And Transmission=Manual Then Set Suspension=Full-Boom.

The response of operation for filter criteria will be as follows:
Criteria: { Group: Engine-Box, Family:-, feature:-} - Rules returned will be 1,2,3,4.

Criteria: { Group: Engine-Box, Family: Engine, feature:Diesel} - Rules returned will be 3.
Criteria: { Group: -, Family: -, feature: Manual} - Rules returned will be 1,3,4.

Operation.description:
This operation splits the given input expressions into the list of model and option condition expressions.
The business object type of the Cfg0AbsValue value objects, with which the input expressions are formed, divides these values into a set of Cfg0AbsModel objects and a set of Cfg0AbsOptionValue objects. This operation decomposes each input expression into a two lists. One expression list that is formed exclusively with Cfg0AbsModel objects and other expression list that is formed exclusively with Cfg0AbsOptionValue objects.
Operation.exceptionCondition: The operation will return a ServiceException if an unknown error occurs. A possible source for unknown errors could be a codeful configurator component customization.
Operation.name: getModelAndOptionConditions
Operation.returnDescription:
Returns the list of the model and the option condition expressions for the given input expressions.
The following partial errors may be returned:
79009 - An invalid configuration perspective is passed to the operation.
79010 - The operation expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
Operation.useCase:
Input expression will be spitted into model and option condition expressions.
Use Case1:
Example: Input expression - "Model=m1 OR Model=m2 AND Engine=e1" is decomposed into 2 lists with 2 elements each.
The model expression list will contain: modelExpressions[0]="Model=m1"
modelExpressions[1]= "Model=m2".
The option condition list will contain: optionConditions[0]= "" (an empty expression representing the Boolean constant TRUE)
optionConditions[1]="Engine=e1".
ORing the AND combinations of each model expression with the option condition at the same index forms an expression that is logically equivalent to the input expression:
ModelExpression[0] & OptionCondition[0] | ModelExpression[1] & OptionCondition[1] == InputExpression
Use Case2:
Example: InputExpression= "OF1 = V1 AND (ModelFamily = M1 OR ModelFamily = M3) AND OF3 = V3)"
The Output will contain two list corresponding to the input expression. One list will correspond to the model expression and the other list will correspond to the option condition expression.
ModelExpression will contain: modelExpressions[0]="ModelFamily=M1"
modelExpressions[1]="ModelFamily=M3"
Variant condition list will contain: optionConditions[0]= " OF1=V1 & OF3=V3"
optionConditions[1]= " OF1=V1 & OF3=V3"

The product item "Car" has following option families and product models LXI,VXI,LDI and VDI in model family "Models". The product item also has summary models created "Petrol Models" and "Diesel Models" in summary model family "Summaries".

User can use operation getModelsForProduct as follows:

If user wants to get all models i.e. product models and summary models, the parameter leafLevelOnly should be passed as FALSE.

If user wants get only product models i.e. LXI,VXI,LDI and VDI, the parameter leafLevelOnly should be passed as TRUE.

The list of family group instances. This parameter is optional. If specified, only the families which are members of the specified family groups within the specified context are returned.

If this parameter is set to true, the families those are not the members of any family group within the specified context are returned.
The default value for this parameter is false, which guides the operation to return the families only from the specified family groups.
Note: This functionality is not supported in the Teamcenter 10.1.2 release.

If this parameter is set to true, the option families those are members of any of the specified groups and are allocated to specified product context are returned even if their availability rule is in an 'unavailable' state.
Default value for this parameter is false.
Note: This functionality is not supported in the Teamcenter 10.1.2 release.

Operation.description:
This internal operation returns the option family instances given context information. If the product item(s) member is provided in context, then the option families that are allocated to any of the specified product item(s) are returned. If the product models member is provided in context, then the option families that are made available to at least one of given the product model(s) are returned.

In addition, to filter the option families further, the 'groups' input parameter can be leveraged. If this parameter is populated with the family group instances or IDs, then the option families that are allocated to any of the specified product item(s) and which are members of the specified family group instances are returned.
If the parameter 'otherFamilies' is set to 'true', then operation will return that option families which are not the members of any family group instances however are allocated to at least one of the specified product item(s).
The default value for this parameter is 'false', which guides the system to only return the Option Families from the Family Groups specified in the input parameter 'groups'.
If parameter 'unavailableFamilies' is set to true, option families those are the members of any of the specified groups and are allocated to specified product context are returned even if their availability rule is in an 'unavailable' state.

Note: In Teamcenter 10.1.2 the product model(s) member of context is ignored.

ParameterInfo.description: An object containing input information required to compute the availability of features to models.

Operation.description: This operation computes the available features within a set of requested families and models. The parameters criteriaExpression and familiesToTest are used to pass in the input expression representing a model and families of interest for which available features are requested. The operation response returns the available product variability for all the features in the requested families, if the features satisfy the input expression in criteriaExpression and the constraint(s) present in the system. The input parameter criteriaExpression is required to contain expression representing models. Iif they don't the the criteriaExpression is empty the operation throws an  error, . The input parameter familiesToTest is required to contain list of Family. If the requested family list is empty, the operation throws an error.
Operation.name: getOptionValueAvailability
Operation.returnDescription:
A per model list of variant features, along with the availability status.

The following partial errors may be returned:
    • 77075 - The operation has failed, because at least one Family is expected in the input.
    • 79009 - An invalid configuration perspective is passed to the operation getOptionValueAvailability.
    • 79010 - The operation "getOptionValueAvailability" expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
    • 256054 - The value for the "applyConstraints" bit pattern is invalid. Please refer to documentation for valid values.
Operation.useCase:
Consider the following Variability data in a Configurator Ccontext itemsay "MyProductItem":

Model Family    Features
M
    • m1
    • m2
    • m3


Family    Features
A
    • a1
    • a2
    • a3


B
    • b1
    • b2
    • b3


C
    • c1
    • c2
    • c3


Rules:
    • a1 is available with m1: This is anavailability rule stating that the configuration feature a1 (of the family A) is available with the model m1 (of model family M).
    • a2 is available with m1: This is an availability rule stating that the configuration feature a2 (of the family A) is available with the model m1 (of model family M).
    • b1 is available with m2: This is an availability rule stating that the configuration feature b1 (of the family B) is available with the model m2 (of model family M).

criteriaExpression = { M=m1}
familiesToTest = {A}
applyConstraints = 1(enable configurator constraint evaluation)

Response -
For Model M1 - a1(Available ) , a2(Available ), a3( Not Available )

Operation.useCase:
An application wants to qualify variant conditions that were retrieved with getVariantExpressions as to whether the condition is equal to, intersects with, or is a subset or superset of the variant criteria associated with the currently active variant configuration criteria (VariantRule). This cannot be achieved with properties on variant conditions or VariantRules because the result depends on the combination of a variant condition and the variant configuration criteria on a VariantRule. One and the same condition may have different overlap states with different VariantRules.
The application calls getOverlapStates and passes the variant criteria (as obtained from a VariantRule using getVariantExpressions) as referenceExpression, and the variant conditions (as obtained from a set of product data elements using getVariantExpressions) as expressions.

Operation.description:
This operation returns the product defaults for the input expression(s) by applying the default rule(s). The revision rule is used to determine the correct revision of configurator objects like rules, families, features, availability statements etc, that take part in the process. The parameter expressionsToUpdate specifies the input variant expressions for the variant configuration. The parameter families specifies the option families for which a default value assignment is requested. If specified, the server assigns default features for only these families in the response. If the list is empty, the server assigns default features for all the families.

This operation also returns the list of mandatory families, which do not have any value selection. The response returns this list of families in parameter requiredFamilies. The parameter criteriaStatus conveys the information about the status of the configuration.
Operation.exceptionCondition: No error conditions result at this time for this operation.
Operation.name: getProductDefaults
Operation.returnDescription:
The response is the expression obtained by applying satisfying default rules, which does not conflict with any other constraint in the system.
However default rules will be applied on the branches which has satisfying default rules without conflicting with other constraint in that branch.
    • The following partial errors may be returned:77034 - The supported variant expression types for the object "Rule 001" of type "Default Rule" are 27, 33. Invalid variant expression types provided : 38
    • 79010 - The operation "getProductDefaults" expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
    • 256054 - The value for the applyDefaults bit pattern is invalid.
Operation.useCase:
Consider the following Variability data in a Configurator context :
Family Features
TYPE CLASSIC, HATCHBACK, SEDAN
ENGINE L4, V6, V8
COLOR RED, GREEN, BLUE
ABS ABS
Default Rules:
Default Rule 1 - "If TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4 then Apply COLOR=RED"
Default Rule 2 - "If TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4 then Apply ABS=TRUE"
The getProductDefaults operation can be used in following ways:

Example 1:
User provides the input expression to getProductDefaults as "TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4" then the response will be "TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4 and COLOR=RED and ABS=TRUE" in expressionsWithDefaults. The parameter requiredfamilies will be blank and the parameter criteiaStatus has value validAndComplete.

Example 2:
User provides input expression to getProductDefaults as TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4, the input parameter families contains family COLOR. The response returns the variant expression as "TYPE=CLASSIC and ENGINE=L4 and COLOR=RED". ABS=TRUE is not expected in the response because family ABS didn't exist in the input parameter families. The parameter requiredfamilies will contain "ABS" and the parameter criteriaStatus has value validAndInComplete.

Example 3:
User provides input expression to getProductDefaults as TYPE=HATCHBACK and ENGINE=L4, the input parameter families contains family as COLOR. The response will have the variant expression as "TYPE=HATCHBACK and ENGINE=L4". The parameter requiredfamilies will contain the Family COLOR and the parameter criteriaStatus has value validAndInComplete. Consider the following Variability data in a Configurator context : Family Values Models VXI, LXI TYPE CLASSIC, HATCHBACK, SEDAN
Availability Rules: "TYPE = CLASSIC" is available to "Models = VXI" "TYPE = SEDAN" is available to "Models = LXI" Default Rules: Default Rule 1: "TYPE = SEDAN".

Example 4:
User provides input expression to getProductDefaults as "Models = VXI | Models = LXI". The response will have the variant expression as "Models = VXI | Models = LXI & TYPE = SEDAN". Here we have two branches in the input criteria expression. The first branch is "Models = VXI" and the second branch is "Models = LXI". As SEDAN is not available to VXI and it is available to LXI, default rule gets applied to second branch only.
The parameter requiredfamilies will contain blank and the parameter criteriaStatus has value validAndComplete.

Operation.description:
This operation returns variability data for an input Configurator perspective. It allows a caller to filter the data based in input criteria.
The returned variability is comprised of one or more of the following objects configured by an input Configurator Perspective.
•    Groups (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup)
•    Families and Feature Families (Cfg0AbsOptionFamily and Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily)
•    Features and Standalone Features (Cfg0AbsOptionValue and Cfg0AbsFeature)
•    Model Families, Product Line Families and Summary Model Families (Cfg0AbsModelFamily)
•    Models (Cfg0AbsModel) including “Product Model” (Cfg0AbsProductModel), “Product Line” (Cfg0AbsProductLine), and “Summary Model” (Cfg0AbsSummaryModel)

The purpose of this SOA operation is to provide a convenient way for clients to link group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup) workspace objects with their family (Cfg0AbsFamily) workspace objects and family workspace objects with their feature (Cfg0AbsValue) workspace objects for the input configurator perspective. It also provides the corresponding allocation (Cfg0AbsAssociation) objects through which the group, family and feature objects are associated with the underlying configurator context item.
The Revision Rule in the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective->cfg0RevisionRule) only considers candidate revisions, that meet the following criteria:
    1.    Read Access: Candidate revisions with read access are considered for revision rule configuration.
    2.    Configuration Date: The revision date predates the rule date (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective->cfg0RevisionRule->rule_date). The relevant revision date depends on the “revision rule clause”:
        a.    “Any Status” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on the “Date Released” of the revision (WorkspaceObject->date_released)
        b.    “Selected Status” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on “Date Released” of the selected Release Status (WorkspaceObject->release_status_list->date_released)
        c.    “Working” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on “Creation Date” of the revision (WorkspaceObject->creation_date)
    3.    Effective Date: If the Revision Rule specifies effectivity criteria, then only candidate revisions that are effective for the given effectivity criteria are considered for configuring a valid revision. Effectivity dates can refer to the future dates. The Effectivity date is expected to specify a date later than the rule date, but the system does not enforce this expectation. You only need to configure for an effectivity date that precedes the rule date if you are making changes that are expected to take effect prior to saving these changes. For example, this can be done if you are cataloging archeological artifacts.

ParameterInfo.description: Recipe for executing the search
Search Options for a given Search (load count and sorting)

Operation.description:
Executes a search based on a search recipe. The search results can contain any sub-types of POM_Object. The search recipe could be a complex search definition that combines multiple simpler search definitions in a logical sequence, e.g. multiple saved queries as defined in the Teamcenter application QueryBuilder.

The search is executed in the context of a configurator perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective). Configurator objects such as features, or constraint rules, are filtered based on their relationship to the product context items and product models in the configurator perspective.

Variant and effecitvity configurable objects in the search results are filtered according to the criteria associated with the VariantRule and RevisionRule in the configurator perspective.

Revisable objects in the search results are revision configured according to the RevisionRule in the configurator perspective.

The results of a search are returned in batches based on the defaultLoadCount specified in the search options. A search cursor object is returned in the response with which subsequent batches can be requested with operation fetchNextSearchResults.

Search options may be used to sort the results of a search using one or more attributes of the returned objects.
Operation.exceptionCondition: No error conditions result at this time for this operation.
Operation.name: executeSearch
Operation.returnDescription:
The found objects and the search cursor object for retrieving next set of objects. The partial errors are returned for following case

    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided.
    • 79008 - The search criteria provided in input is invalid.
Operation.useCase:
1. Get models for product. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve, searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries contains a saved query for searching models.

2. Get Family Groups. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspective; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries contains a saved query for searching Family Groups.

3. Get Option Families. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries contains a saved query for searching families.

4. Get Option Values. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries will have a saved query for searching features.

5. Get Derived Default Rules. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries will have a saved query for searching derived default rules, searchRecipe.searchExpression.filterCriteria will have the filter information.

6. Get Exclude Rules. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries will have a saved query for searching exclude rules, searchRecipe.searchExpression.filterCriteria will have the filter information.

7. Get Include Rules. Provide product context, revision rule and filter list in parameter searchRecipe.configuratorPerspecitve; searchRecipe.searchExpression.savedQueries will have a saved query for searching include rules,searchRecipe.searchExpression.filterCriteria will have the filter information.

Operation.useCase:
This operation can be used to display formulae for ConfigExpression structures returned by getVariantExpressions operation. The examples of display formulae are as follows:
(NS is family namespace)

1)    Boolean expression

    • [NS]!BOOL - reprepsents FALSE


2)    Date expressions
    • [NS]REL_DATE = 22-Jan-2013 00:00     (dd-mmm-yyyy HH:SS)


3)    Range expressions
    • [NS]A = a1 & [NS]LENGTH <= 50
    • [NS]A = a1 & ([NS]LENGTH >= 1 & [NS]LENGTH <= 10)
    • [NS]A = a1 & [NS]LENGTH >= 20
    • [NS]A = a1 & !([NS]LENGTH >= 20)

5)    Multiple selections within a single column

ParameterInfo.description: A list of VariantRule objects or subtype objects for which the configuration information and/or variant expression is to be returned.

A list of request names and value pairs.
The valid name-values are:
•    mode – Represents the request mode that specifies what information on VariantRule objects is to be returned for a request.
Supported values are:
1.    “expression” : Return variant expression information only in response.
2.    “configurationProfile” : Return configuration profile information only in response.
3.    “expressionAndConfigurationProfile” : Return variant expression and configuration profile information in response.
             Default mode is “expression”.
•    expressionType – Represents an Integer value that specifies the type of expression on VariantRule to be returned in response. This request information is valid only for modes “expression” or “expressionAndConfigurationProfile”.
Supported values are:
1.    “18” : Configurator criteria expression based on user selections and system selections.
2.    “48” : Configurator criteria expression based on user selected features.
             Default expressionType is “18”.

Operation.description:
This operation returns variant expression and/or configuration information associated with the input VariantRule objects.
User criteria expression or expanded expression is returned based on the expressionType from requestInfo. Configuration information is returned as a combination of Configurator perspective which holds the product information and Solve Profile which holds parameters to govern the constraint evaluation behavior.
Operation.name: getVariantInformation
Operation.returnDescription:
Returns the variant expression and configuration information present on input VariantRule objects. If operation fails to retrieve variant expression or session information for an input object, a partial error is returned for the same and the processing continues for the next object in the list.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    79014 - Some or all of the key-value pairs in the list of request info pairs sent to the operation "getVariantInformation" are unsupported: "{ key=invalidkey1 : values = [ invalidvalue1 ]}".
•    79015 - The operation “getVariantInformation” has failed to retrieve configuration information for VariantRule at index “n".
•    79016 - The operation “getVariantInformation” has failed to retrieve variant information for VariantRule at index “n”.
•    79017 - The operation “getVariantInformation” expects atleast one Variant Rule in the input.
Operation.useCase:
User can get the user expression or expanded expression stored on VariantRule objects and may also use this information to compare variant expressions on these objects. User wants to get configuration information stored on the VariantRule objects.
User may also use this information along with the Criteria to apply on product content and configure it. The configuration information will represent a snapshot of features and constraints against which the criteria will be evaluated.


Consider the following variability data in a Positive Biased Product Context:

Car_Product_Context
Group        Family        Features
Model
                Luxury
                Economy
Car_Group
Battery
                48kWh
                64kWh
                72kWh
Color
                White
                Black
Airbags FreeForm Family with minimum value as 1 & maximum value as 6.

Rules:
Include Rule – If ‘Model=Luxury’ then include ‘Battery=64kWh’.
Include Rule – If ‘Model=Economy’ then includes ‘Battery=48kWh’.
Default Rule – If ‘Model=Luxury’ then default to ‘Color=Black’.
Exclude Rule – If ‘Model=Economy’ then exclude ‘Airbag>4’.

Saved Variant Rules:
SVR_Luxury: Model=Luxury & Airbags=4 & Battery=64kWh & Color=Black
where selection for Battery and Color is system selected.

SVR_Economy: Model=Economy & Airbags>3 & Battery=48kWh
where selection for Battery family is system selected.

Use case 1:
Get the expanded expression information for the Variant Rules.

Input:
targetObjects = [SVR_Luxury, SVR_Economy]
requestInfo    = [mode=[“expression”],
                         expressionType=[“18”]]

Response:
The response contains the following information:

1.    The variant expression JSON containing the expanded expression on the input Variant Rules, below is the formula on the expression:
SVR_Luxury: Color=Black & Airbags=4 & Battery=64kWh & Model=Luxury
SVR_Economy: (Airbags>3) & Battery=48kWh & Model=Economy
This JSON string adheres to the JSON schema for variant expression defined in VariantExpression_Schema.json located in %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema.

2.    The variability tree data containing nodes for variability referenced in the variant expressions:
Products_Group
    Model
         Economy
             Luxury
Car_Group
    Battery
         48kWh
             64kWh
    Color
         Black
    Airbags
         4
         >3

3.    The view model object map containing the requested objects and its properties. It also contains the properties for variant data present in the variability tree.


Use case 2:
Get the configuration profile information for the Variant Rules.

Input:
targetObjects = [SVR_Luxury, SVR_Economy]
requestInfo    = [mode=[“configurationProfile”],
                         properties=[“cfg0VariantRuleText”, “object_desc”]]


Response:
The response contains the following information:

1.    The solve profile JSON containing the solve profile key and values for the input Variant Rules:
SVR_Luxury:     CFG_PROFILE_applyConfigConstraints = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_violationComputationTimeout = 4
                 CFG_PROFILE_minErrorSeverity = Error
                 CFG_PROFILE_minReportSeverity = Error
                 CFG_PROFILE_validateWithoutExpand = true
SVR_Economy: CFG_PROFILE_applyConfigConstraints = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_violationComputationTimeout = 4
                 CFG_PROFILE_minErrorSeverity = Error
                 CFG_PROFILE_minReportSeverity = Error
                 CFG_PROFILE_validateWithoutExpand = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_applyDefaults = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_considerLowSeverityRulesForExpansion = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_preferEmptyValueForDiscretionary = true
                 CFG_PROFILE_reportViolationForMutuallyExclusiveConstraint = true

This JSON string adheres to the JSON schema for solve profile defined in SolveProfile_Schema.json located in %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema. For details regarding each solve profile key, please refer booleanmath/cfg_tokens.h.

2.The view model object map containing the requested objects. For this use case, the propeties contain the configuration perspective information including the product item, revision rule and rule date information.

ParameterInfo.description: A Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective is a runtime business object representing a snapshot of a Configurator Product Context object. The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.

A list of rule type names. Objects corresponding to these rule types will be returned. If the list is empty, objects of all rule types will be returned. Note that the object needs to be a subtype of Cfg0AbsRule.
A list of families and features that are part of the condition expression. The object must be a subtype of either Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue.
A list of families and features that are part of the subject expression. The object must be subtype of either Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue.

A QueryInput. This is an optional parameter for a saved search query. When executed, the query should return an object of the type Cfg0AbsRule. The query can be based on the out-of-the-box (OOTB) attributes of Cfg0AbsRule or any custom attributes of custom classes. The operation intersects the result of the query with the results of other criteria specified in this operation, such as ruleTypes, conditions, and subject. This means the final result is based on both the query and these additional criteria. Please refer to the use cases for examples. If this parameter is not specified, the operation will search based on other input parameter criteria.

A list of KeyValuePair. This is an optional input parameter. Supported key is ‘matchAllObjects’. This key is used to search for a rule based on whether all or anyof the input conditions or subject need to be present in the rule’s conditions or subject respectively. The valid values are:
•    true :    All specified conditions and subject need to be present in the rule’s conditions and subjects. This is a default value.
•    false :    Any of the specifed subject and condtions is present in the rule’s conditions and subjects

Operation.description:
Retrieves an array of Configurator rules for a given configurator perspective, based on the criteria as specified below.

You can specify abstract or concrete classes for filtering, all of which must be subtypes of Cfg0AbsRule.

List of families and features referenced in a rule’s expression. The type of the expression can be either 'condition' or 'subject'.
The families or features may be referenced in the expression using the logical operators 'AND', 'OR', or 'NOT'. Depending on the requirement, all or any of the families and features in this list may need to be referenced in the expression for the constraint to qualify for the output list. The expression may reference additional families or features beyond those in the input list.
If you specify that all the input families or features need to be referenced in the rule's condition expression and if one or more families or features from this list are not referenced, then the constraint will not qualify for output. If you specify that any of the input families or features can be referenced to in the rule's condition expression, the constraint will qualify if any of the input families or features are present in the constraint's condition expression.
The same search process is applied when searching families and features in a subject expression.

For rules of the type Cfg0AbsFreeFormRule, their features and families are considered as the subject.

A saved query with a list of persistent attributes and their values. These attributes can be either custom attributes or out-of-the-box (OOTB) attributes.
Operation.name: searchConstraints
Operation.returnDescription:
The operation returns a search constraint response.

Following partial errors may be returned.
3005 - Invalid attribute 'text' found for query.
3020 - No value was specified for this query.
3040 - This query cannot be executed.
77073 - The Configurator Perspective is invalid.
77199 - Input to the property 'text' for "searchConditions" should be of type 'Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue' or Cfg0AbsRule
79014 - Some or all of the key-value pairs in the list of request info pairs sent to the operation "text" are unsupported: "text". Please report this error to your system administrator.
Operation.useCase:
Consider the following data,
Configurator Context: Car (Positive Bias)
    Models: Standard, Luxury
    Families:
        Battery: 80kWh, 90kWh, 100kWh (Single Select, String Family)
        Sunroof: Yes, No (Boolean Family)
        Accessories: Bluetooth, Touchscreen, Mobileholder (Multi Select, String Family)
        Color: Red, Blue, Silver (Dynamic Family, Single Select with Standalone features)
        Airbags: 4, 6 (Single Select Integer)
    
1.    Include Rule (R1)
        a.    Condition: [Car]Models = Luxury
        b.    Subject: [Car] Sunroof = Sunroof & [Car]Accessories = Bluetooth & [Car]Accessories = Touchscreen
2.    Exclude Rule (R2)
        a.    Condition: [Car]Models = Standard
        b.    Subject: [Car]Battery=100kWh & [Car]Color=Silver
3.    Include Rule (R3)
        a.    Condition: [Car] Battery = 100kWh
        b.    Subject: [Car]Sunroof = Sunroof & [Car]Accessories = Touchscreen & [Car]Accessories = Mobileholder
4.    Include Rule (R4)
        a.    Condition: [Car]Models = Standard & ([Car] Battery = 80kWh || [Car] Battery = 90 kWh)
        b.    Subject: [Car]Sunroof != Sunroof & [Car]Airbags = 4
5.    FreeForm Rule (R5)
        a.    Free form expression = "(assert (=> (and (= |[Car]Battery| "100kWh") (= |[Car]Color| "Silver")) (= |[Car]Sunroof| true)))"
6.    Matrix Rule (R6)
        a.    Condition: [Car]Models = Luxury
        b.    Subject: Features = {Color, Red, Blue, Silver, Battery, 80kWh, 100kWh},
                     Feature Disposition = Silver (Optional), Red (Optional), Blue (Optional), Color (Mandatory)


Example 1.
Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. ruletype = “Cfg0IncludeRule”
c. conditions = Luxury
d. subject = Sunroof, Touchscreen
e. queryInput = Empty
f. matchAllObjects = true

Output1: R1

Example 2.
Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. ruletype = Empty
c. conditions = 80kWh, Luxury
d. subject = Sunroof, 4 (Airbags)
e. queryInput = Empty
f. matchAllObjects = false

Output: R4

Example 3.
Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. ruletype = Empty
c. conditions = Empty
d. subject = Silver
e. queryInput = Empty
f. matchAllObjects = true

Output: R2,R6

Example 4:
To use the operation with the 'queryInput' parameter, you need to have a saved query in the Teamcenter system. You will need to create an object of a specific type, which is QueryInput.

A sample saved query might look like this:
Saved query name = "__Cfg0testSavedQuery"
Query clauses: SELECT uid FROM Cfg0AbsRule WHERE "Name" = "<name>"

The input object:
QueryInput samplQueryInput;
samplQueryInput.query = IManQuery of "__Cfg0testSavedQuery”
samplQueryInput.entries = {“Name”}
samplQueryInput.values = {“R3”}

Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. Ruletype = Empty
c. conditions = Empty
d. subject = Sunroof
e. queryInput = samplQueryInput
f. matchAllObjects = true

Output: R3

Explaination:
From the samplQueryInput, output(O1)={R3}
From the subject criteria, output(O2)={R1, R3, R4}
Final output = Intersection of (O1) & (O2) = {R3}

Note that if the output of the sampleQueryInput is empty, the final output will also be empty, even if there are results from other criteria.

Example 5.
Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. ruletype = “Cfg0MatrixRule”
c. conditions = Luxury
d. subject = Silver
e. queryInput = Empty
f. matchAllObjects = true

Output: R6

Example 6.
Input:
a. Car’s Perspective
b. ruletype = “Cfg0FreeFormRule”
c. conditions = Empty
d. subject = Silver, SunRoof
e. queryInput = Empty
f. matchAllObjects = true

Output: R5
Note: For rules of the type Cfg0AbsFreeFormRule, their features and families are considered as the subject.

Operation.useCase:
Use Cases:
The expandAndUpdateVariants operation should expands the input Variant Rules and update expressions along with session information.
Consider the following variability data in a Positive Biased Product Context:

Car_Product_Context
